translationRepairs: Emperor Wu had seven sons. Lady Zhang gave birth to Shaodi; Sun Xiuhua to Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen; the Jieyu Lady Hu to Emperor Wen; Lady Wang Xiurong to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; Lady Yuan to Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia, Yigong; Lady Sun to Prince Yixuan of Nanjun; and Lady Lü to Prince Wen of Hengyang, Yiji.

Emperor Wu had seven sons. Lady Zhang gave birth to Shaodi; Sun Xiuhua to Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen; the Jieyu Lady Hu to Emperor Wen; Lady Wang Xiurong to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; Lady Yuan to Prince Wenxian of Jiangxia, Yigong; Lady Sun to Prince Yixuan of Nanjun; and Lady Lü to Prince Wen of Hengyang, Yiji.
The Chinese gives the posthumous name 文獻 (Wenxian), not Wuxian: 江夏文獻王義恭. The literal field has the same error ("Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia Yigong").
General Who Establishes Might Fu Hongzhi said, 'Your orders were to press on quickly, for fear the barbarians would overtake and slaughter the men.
General Who Establishes Might Fu Hongzhi said, 'The Duke's orders were to press on quickly, for fear the barbarians would overtake and slaughter the men.
公處分亟進: 公 refers to the Duke (Gaozu), whose standing orders were to advance quickly; Fu Hongzhi is not quoting his listeners' orders. The literal field ("Your orders were") has the same error.
At that time many people from upstream Longyou who had fled were living in Guanzhong, hoping that the dynasty's great prestige would let them return home.
At that time many refugees from the Long uplands were living in Guanzhong, hoping that the dynasty's great prestige would let them return home.
隴上流人 means refugees from the Long uplands (隴上); 上 here is part of the toponym, not "upstream". The literal field ("refugees from upstream Longyou") has the same error.
When Duke Gongshu was not removed, he nearly overturned the state of Zheng;
When Gongshu was not removed, he nearly overturned the state of Zheng;
共叔 is Gongshu Duan, younger brother of Duke Zhuang of Zheng; he was never a duke, so "Duke Gongshu" mistranslates the name. The literal field has the same error.
when Liu Ying was indulgently kept alive, the omen spread and the trouble ran deep.
when Liu Ying was indulgently kept alive, the rift widened and the trouble ran deep.
釁 here means a breach or fault (釁廣難深, the rift widened and the trouble deepened), not an omen. The literal field has the same error.

Yet before Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Xing Antai and General of Broad Might Mao Zhongsi he allowed their insolent abuse, mocking the ruler and slandering the court—conduct long known near and far and exposed to all.

Yet before Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Xing Antai and General of Broad Might Mao Zhongsi he gave free rein to insolent abuse, mocking the ruler and slandering the court—conduct long known near and far and exposed to all.

縱其悖罵: 其 is Yizhen himself, who unleashed abuse in the envoys' presence; "allowed their insolent abuse" reverses the referent. 散騎侍郎 is Attendant Gentleman, not Regular Attendant (散騎常侍), of the Scattered Cavalry. The literal field has both errors.
Thus Kaoshu revoked his oath at the Yellow Spring, and the magistrate of Huguan restored a wronged soul at Huyi.
Thus Kaoshu brought about the reversal of the oath sworn about the Yellow Spring, and the elder of Huguan restored a wronged soul at Huyi.

The oath (不及黃泉) was Duke Zhuang of Zheng's; Kaoshu caused it to be reversed, so "revoked his oath" is wrong. 壺關 alludes to the elder of Huguan who defended the wronged Han crown prince; no magistrate is meant. The literal field misreads 壺關 as a bare name.

I bow before Gaozu the Martial Emperor, who brought forth divine martial power and seized the turning fortune as the dragon rose. Looking up he cleared the heavenly steps to match the virtue of Shun's Yu; looking down he swept the Nine Regions to rival the achievement of the Great Xia. Reverently following Heaven and man, he held the realm.

I bow before Gaozu the Martial Emperor, who brought forth divine martial power and seized the turning fortune as the dragon rose. Looking up he cleared the heavenly steps to match the virtue of Shun of Youyu; looking down he swept the Nine Regions to rival the achievement of the Great Xia. Reverently following Heaven and man, he held the realm.
有虞 is Youyu, the clan or realm of the sage ruler Shun; "Shun's Yu" garbles it. The literal field's "Yu of Shun" reverses the elements.
On the guimwei day of the sixth month of the second year of Jingping, Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues sent agents to kill Yizhen at his place of exile; he was eighteen.
On the guiwei day of the sixth month of the second year of Jingping, Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues sent agents to kill Yizhen at his place of exile; he was eighteen.
The sexagenary day 癸未 is romanized guiwei; "guimwei" is a corrupted spelling. The literal field has the same error.

In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanjia an edict said, "The former coffin of the Prince of Luling lies far away and his state fief lies in ruin; moved to grief and anguish, my feelings are as if pierced through.

In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanjia an edict said, "The coffin of the former Prince of Luling lies far away and his state fief lies in ruin; moved to grief and anguish, my feelings are as if pierced through.
前廬陵王靈柩: 前 qualifies the prince (the former Prince of Luling), not the coffin. The literal field has the same misplacement.
In old times Guan the Elder presented a memorial and was recorded in Han annals; Yan Zuan offered remonstrance and was honored in Jin.
In old times the Elder of Huguan presented a memorial and was recorded in Han annals; Yan Zuan offered remonstrance and was honored in Jin.
關老 abbreviates the Three Elders of Huguan (壺關三老), who memorialized for the wronged Han crown prince; Guan is a place, not a surname. The literal field has the same error.
Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia, Yigong, was clever and bright from childhood, with a beautiful countenance; Gaozu especially cherished him, and none of the other sons could compare.
Prince Wenxian of Jiangxia, Yigong, was clever and bright from childhood, with a beautiful countenance; Gaozu especially cherished him, and none of the other sons could compare.
The posthumous name is 文獻 (Wenxian), not Wuxian: 江夏文獻王義恭.
The princes of Luling never dared to ask; if they asked they did not receive.
The Prince of Luling and the other princes never dared to ask; if they asked they did not receive.
廬陵諸王 means the Prince of Luling (Yizhen) and the other princes; there were not several "princes of Luling". The literal field has the same error.
Ximen Bao and An Yu reformed their natures to equal beauty;
Ximen Bao and Dong Anyu reformed their natures to equal beauty;
安於 is Dong Anyu (董安于), paired with Ximen Bao in the classic example of correcting one's temperament; "An Yu" misreads the given name as a full name.

If affairs differ from today and the heir is young and tender, the Director of Retainers will then have the affairs of the Duke of Zhou—you must not fail to fulfill the principle of reverent obedience.

If affairs differ from today and the heir is young and tender, the Minister over the Masses will then have the affairs of the Duke of Zhou—you must not fail to fulfill the principle of reverent obedience.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses; Director of Retainers translates a different office (司隸校尉). The literal field has the same error.
In year twenty he was sent out as General of the Guard and Governor of Jiangzhou, aged twelve.
In year twenty he was sent out as General of the Southern Household and Governor of Jiangzhou, aged twelve.
南中郎將 is the General of the Southern Household (Southern Gentlemen of the Palace), not a guard general. The literal field has the same error.
In year twenty-two he came to court, received halberds, and was made commander over the military affairs of Xiyang, Jinxing, and Xincai in Jiang and Yu.
In year twenty-two he came to court, received halberds, and was made commander over the military affairs of Xiyang, Jinxi, and Xincai in Jiang and Yu.
The commandery 晉熙 is Jinxi; "Jinxing" is a misreading. The literal field has the same error.
With no son, in Taishi year one Emperor Ming made Ziyu, styled Xiaowen, twenty-first son of Xiaowu and Prince of Jinxi, Shao's heir and Prince of Luling.
With no son, in Taishi year one Emperor Ming made Ziyu, Prince of Jinxi, styled Xiaowen, twenty-first son of Xiaowu, Shao's heir and Prince of Luling.

In 世祖第二十一子晉熙王子輿 the Prince of Jinxi is Ziyu himself; "son of Xiaowu and Prince of Jinxi" can be read as making Xiaowu the Prince of Jinxi. The literal field is garbled ("Ziyu of Prince Ziyu of Jinxi").
In year three Desi, second son of Prince Xiufan of Guiyang, was made Shao's heir.
In year three De, second son of Prince Xiufan of Guiyang, was made Shao's heir.
德嗣紹 means De (德) succeeded Shao; 嗣 is the verb (compare 繼紹 in s0490), so the name is not "Desi". The literal field has the same error.
In year three Hao, styled Yuanhua, third son of Marquis Zhong of Linli, was adopted to succeed Shao.
In year three Hao, styled Yuanhua, third son of Xi, Marquis Zhong of Linli, was adopted to succeed Shao.
臨澧忠侯襲 includes the marquis's personal name 襲 (Xi), which the translation omits. The literal field omits it too.
給事中 is a single office (Gentleman Attendant); "Gentlemen" is a grammatical error. The literal field ("Made Gentlemen Attendant.") has the same error.
In year three he supervised military affairs in Southern Xu and Yan and Jincheng in Yangzhou as Governor of Xuzhou, with commission and rank unchanged.
In year three he supervised military affairs in Southern Xu and Yan and Jinling in Yangzhou as Governor of Xuzhou, with commission and rank unchanged.
The commandery 晉陵 is Jinling; "Jincheng" is a misreading. The literal field has the same error.
Yigong dabbled in letters but was proud and extravagant; once he left for his post Taizu wrote to warn him: You at weak crown already hold a frontier command in person.
Yigong dabbled in letters but was proud and extravagant; once he left for his post Taizu wrote to warn him: Barely of capping age, you already hold a regional command in person.
弱冠 is an idiom for barely reaching the capping age (about twenty); the calque "at weak crown" obscures the meaning. The literal field has the same calque.

When urgent business is judged and finished, you may then enter to inquire after us; having seen our countenance and examined how we rise and rest, you should go out at once and not stay long, lest common affairs be neglected.

When urgent business is judged and finished, you may then go in to pay your respects to the Grand Consort; having seen her countenance and asked after her health, you should go out at once and not stay long, lest common affairs be neglected.

入問訊…既睹顏色，審起居 describes Yigong visiting the Grand Consort (his mother, provided for in s0159) at his post; Taizu, writing from the capital, is not the one visited, so "us/our" is a wrong referent. The literal field has the same error.
The Director of Retainers says the same.
The Minister over the Masses says the same.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses; Director of Retainers translates 司隸校尉. The literal field has the same error.

In the ninth year he was recalled as commander over the military affairs of Southern Yan, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You and of Liang commandery in Yuzhou, General Who Campaigns North, Grand Marshal with the ceremony of the three excellencies, and governor of Southern Yan, garrisoning Guangling.

In the ninth year he was recalled as commander over the military affairs of Southern Yan, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You and of Liang commandery in Yuzhou, General Who Campaigns North, Grand Master with honours equal to the Three Excellencies, and governor of Southern Yan, garrisoning Guangling.
開府儀同三司 is the honour of opening an office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies; "Grand Marshal" (太尉) is a different post. The literal field has the same error.
The discernment of Duke Wu of Zhao was proved in managing the granaries.
The discernment of Zhao Wu was shown in the men he recommended from among the storehouse keepers.
趙武 is Zhao Wu (Zhao Wenzi), a minister of Jin, not a duke; 事彰管庫 alludes to the men he promoted from the storehouse keepers (管庫之士), not to managing granaries. The literal field is vague but not wrong.
In winter of year twenty-nine he returned to the capital; Xiaowu came out on the imperial dark-hawk boat to welcome him.
In winter of year twenty-nine he returned to the capital; the Emperor came out on the imperial dark-hawk boat to welcome him.
In winter of Yuanjia 29 (AD 452) the reigning emperor (上) was Taizu (Emperor Wen); Xiaowu did not take the throne until AD 453. The literal field correctly has "the Emperor".
He went back to hold the Eastern Palace residence.
He went back to hold the Eastern Residence (Dongfu).
東府 is the Eastern Residence, the seat of the chief minister in Jiankang, not the Heir's Eastern Palace (東宮). The literal field has the same error.
Shi Liang's feats shine in the Documents of Yu;
The achievement of timely furthering Heaven's work shines in the Canon of Yu;
時亮 alludes to the Canon of Shun, 惟時亮天功 ("timely further the work of Heaven"); it is not a person, so "Shi Liang" is an invented name. The literal field has the same error.
On a day of leisure they pooled their modest views on what ought to be trimmed, and respectfully set forth nine proposals.
On a day of leisure we have pooled our modest views on what ought to be trimmed, and respectfully set forth nine proposals.
臣等 speak in the first person inside the memorial; "they" breaks the quoted voice of s0299-s0303.
Though doubting their hearts are equal to the task, they hoped at least to offer what little sincerity they had.
Though we fear our hearts are not equal to the task, we hope at least to offer what little sincerity we have.
First-person voice of the memorial (臣等); the display English switches to "they".
They pray that after Your Majesty has heard them, you will graciously accept—so that court and realm may rest secure and inner and outer harmony prevail."
We pray that after Your Majesty has heard them, you will graciously accept—so that court and realm may rest secure and inner and outer harmony prevail."
First-person voice of the memorial (伏願); the display English switches to "they".
Yigong constantly feared Xiaowu's mistrust; when Prince Xiamao of Hailing rose in rebellion at Xiangyang he memorialized, saying:
Yigong constantly feared Xiaowu's mistrust; when Prince Xiumao of Hailing rose in rebellion at Xiangyang he memorialized, saying:
休茂 is romanised Xiumao; "Xiamao" is a misspelling. The literal field has the same error.
Raised in palace depths they never saw the fields; attendants never knew rural toil—wealth and pride came naturally, hairs gathered until the axle snaps, and disaster followed.

Raised in palace depths they never saw sowing and reaping; their attendants and intimates are no Tian Su—wealth, pride and extravagance come naturally, feathers pile up until the axle snaps, and disaster follows.
田蘇 is Tian Su, the worthy of Jin from the Zuo Commentary (無忌…與田蘇遊，而曰好仁); "rural toil" misreads the name. The literal field has the same error.
In year six the Minister over the Masses and Grand Tutor offices were dissolved, but recruitment continued as before.
In year six his headquarters as Minister over the Masses and as Grand Preceptor were dissolved, but he kept recruiting staff as before.
太宰 is the Grand Preceptor named in s0344, not the Grand Tutor (太傅); 解…府 dissolves Yigong's own headquarters. The literal field has the same error.
In Yongguang, though nominally chief minister, he deferred to close favorites such as Dai Fazxing as if he could never catch up.
In Yongguang, though nominally chief minister, he deferred to close favorites such as Dai Faxing as if he could never catch up.
戴法興 is romanised Dai Faxing; "Fazxing" is a misspelling.

Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia Yigong, Bearer of the Credential Staff, Chancellor, Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat and chief of the Masters of Writing; Yuan Jing, Loyal and Fierce Duke of Badong, Grand Commandant and Governor of Southern Yu; Xiang Gong Qingzhi, Minister of Works and Duke of Shixing; and Marquis Su Min of Taoyang, General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong—some harmonized the age through the Way, others gave loyal service in crushing rebellion—let them share temple sacrifice by state rite."

Prince Wenxian of Jiangxia Yigong, Bearer of the Credential Staff, Chancellor, Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat and chief of the Masters of Writing; Yuanjing, Duke Zhonglie (Loyal and Fierce) of Badong, Grand Commandant and Governor of Southern Yu; Qingzhi, Duke Xiang of Shixing and Minister of Works; and Que, Marquis Su of Taoyang, General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong—some harmonized the age through the Way, others gave loyal service in crushing rebellion—let them share temple sacrifice by state rite."
文獻 is Wenxian, not Wuxian; 襄公 is the posthumous title Duke Xiang, not part of the name; 肅侯愨 is Marquis Su, personal name Que (宗愨), not "Min".
In Shengming year two of Emperor Shun Ji of the clansman Kun again succeeded to the fief.
In Shengming year two of Emperor Shun, Ji, son of the clansman Kun, again succeeded to the fief.
琨子績 is "Ji, son of Kun"; the English garbles the apposition.
Tan's brother Yuanliang was Marquis Min of Jiangan.
Tan's brother Yuanliang was Marquis Min of Jiang'an.
In year twenty-four Yiji lay gravely ill; Taizu sent Secretariat Director Xu Zhizhi to see him and recall him to the capital.
In year twenty-four Yiji lay gravely ill; Taizu sent Secretariat Director Xu Zhanzhi to see him and recall him to the capital.
徐湛之 is Xu Zhanzhi; "Zhizhi" drops 湛.
His son Prince Gong Ni, styled Ziqi, succeeded him.
His son Prince Gong Yi, styled Ziqi, succeeded him.
嶷 as a personal name is read Yí (as in Xiao Yi 蕭嶷), not "Ni".
Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was Gaozu's beloved son, a chief minister who in the Daming era stood at the head of court.
The Prince of Jiangxia was Gaozu's beloved son, holding the rank of senior chancellor, and in the Daming era he personally presided at the head of court.
上相 is the rank of senior chancellor; the Chinese gives only 江夏王 without the personal name.
